edge_types.description: OPTIONAL filter by relationship types: REFERENCES, MENTIONS, IMPORTS, USES, CONTAINS, DESCRIBED_BY, ABOUT, SIMILAR_TO.

entity_id.description: The entity ID to get context for (e.g., a file node ID, ticket ID from search results).

entity_type.description: Entity type: File, CodeSymbol, Repository, Ticket, Message, Document, Concept.

focus_query.description: OPTIONAL: Natural language query to rank related entities by relevance. Example: 'authentication bug' ranks auth-related connections higher.

include_content.description: Whether to include entity contents (true) or just metadata (false, default). Set true when you need full context.

max_related.description: Maximum number of related entities to return. Default: 5, Max: 20.

cursor.description: Continuation cursor from a previous truncated call (structuredContent.next). Use with the SAME query and filters.

entity_concepts.description: OPTIONAL filter by named entities (e.g., ['JWT', 'PostgreSQL', 'telara-middleware']). Narrows search precision.

example_resource_id.description: ALTERNATIVE to query: Find resources similar to this example ID. Uses vector similarity across ALL integrations.

integration_types.description: OPTIONAL filter by specific integrations: github, gitlab, jira, slack, notion, confluence. Leave empty to search ALL.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Default: 10, Max: 50.

max_tokens.description: Token budget for the rendered results (default 4000, 200-20000). Results are returned in rank order until the budget is spent; structuredContent.truncated=true and structuredContent.next carry a cursor for the rest.

min_similarity.description: Minimum similarity score (0.0-1.0) when using example_resource_id. Default: 0.8.

people.description: OPTIONAL: only content written by these people, across all their linked accounts. Each value is an email (dana@acme.com) or a platform account (slack:U024BE7LH, gitlab:dokoro). A person who cannot be found returns no results and is listed as not found.

query.description: Natural language query about connected company context or indexed sources. Do not use for generic programming, operating-system, command-line, or editor how-to questions. Examples: 'authentication bugs in our API', 'OAuth implementation in our repositories', 'recent customer support tickets'. Searches across connected integrations.

resource_types.description: OPTIONAL filter by resource types: ticket, code, file, message, document, incident. Leave empty to search all types.

topic_concepts.description: OPTIONAL filter by topics (e.g., ['authentication', 'database design', 'API security']).

blocked.description: Optional. Current blockers with their reason. Replaces the stored list; send an empty list when nothing is blocked any more.

constraints.description: Optional. Requirements or limits the work must respect.

critical_context.description: Optional. Facts the next session must not lose.

decisions.description: Optional. Decisions made, one per item. Kept for the life of the task.

done.description: Optional. Items completed since the last checkpoint, besides the milestone.

in_progress.description: Optional. Work currently in progress. Replaces the stored list.

knowledge_refs.description: Knowledge graph entity IDs (from telara_knowledge_search or telara_traverse) related to this checkpoint. These create permanent links in the knowledge graph.

milestone.description: Description of what was accomplished since the last checkpoint. Include file paths, decisions made, and key findings.

next_steps.description: What should be done next. This helps the next session (or agent) pick up efficiently.

resources.description: Optional. Files, tickets, URLs or entities this work touched.

task_id.description: UUID of the task to checkpoint.

task_tree.description: Updated task checklist. Each item has step (string), status ('pending'|'in_progress'|'done'), and detail (string).

changes_made.description: Specific artifacts created or modified this session (e.g. 'created GitHub issue #42', 'edited src/auth/login.go', 'sent Slack message to #eng').

final_summary.description: Final summary of the completed task. If omitted, the current rolling summary is used.

task_id.description: UUID of the task to complete.

token_estimate.description: Approximate total tokens used this session, rounded to the nearest 1,000 (e.g. 45000 for ~45k tokens). Self-reported -- not a metered count.

anchors.description: Context anchors that ground the task to specific resources.

file_paths.description: Key file paths relevant to this task.

goal.description: Clear description of what this task aims to accomplish. This is shown to future agents resuming the task.

name.description: Short name for the task (max 100 chars). If omitted, derived from the first 100 characters of the goal.

include_completed.description: Include completed and abandoned tasks in the list. Default: false (only active tasks).

include_receipts.description: Also show gateway receipts: tasks the gateway opened to record undescribed work. Default: false (hidden and counted).

limit.description: How many tasks to show. Default 10 (25 in detail mode), at most 25.

mode.description: summary (default): one line per task. detail: goal, summary, checkpoints and recording notes for each task.

query.description: A task UUID reads that exact task without changes; other text filters task name or goal (case-insensitive).

task_id.description: Exact task UUID to read without changing task state. Scoped to this MCP configuration; bypasses list limits and status filters.

handoff_hint.description: Optional one-line hint for whoever resumes, in any client (e.g. "finish the test suite in Cursor"). Shown in the next session's initialize instructions.

progress_notes.description: Human-readable summary of what was accomplished this session.

resume_context.description: What the next session needs to resume cleanly: current state, exact next step, any blockers, relevant file paths or IDs.

task_id.description: UUID of the task to pause.

token_estimate.description: Approximate total tokens used this session, rounded to the nearest 1,000 (e.g. 45000 for ~45k tokens). Self-reported -- not a metered count.

task_id.description: UUID of the task to resume. Use the ID supplied by the user directly; call task_list only when you need to discover an unknown task ID.
